subtitle: When Pepper Bought Guns and Toppled an Empire

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Marthanda Varma standing over a rolled treaty and discarded Dutch cannon on a riverside ghatscape
panels.action: Marthanda Varma stands tall on stone steps by a Kerala backwater, one hand resting on a rolled palm-leaf treaty, Dutch cannons and ships behind him framed by coconut palms and a humid grey sky.

dialogue.text: In 1753 at Mavelikkara, a pepper king forced the Dutch to sell him guns and abandon power—how did a small coastal kingdom bend a European company to its will?

i18n.hi: १७५३ में मावेलिक्कारा में, एक मिर्च राजा ने डचों से बंदूकें बिकवाईं और सत्ता छोड़वाई — एक छोटे से तटीय राज्य ने यूरोपीय कम्पनी को कैसे झुका लिया?

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Malabar coast with ports glowing in the dusk
panels.action: A sweeping aerial view shows the Malabar coast at dusk, dotted with small harbours, spice godowns and anchored European ships along a line of coconut-fringed beaches and backwaters.

dialogue.text: For a century, the Malabar coast was a chain of ports where pepper drew Europe across the seas and the Dutch VOC ruled with forts, contracts and cannon.

i18n.hi: सौ साल तक, मलबार तट पर बंदरगाहों की कड़ी थी, जहाँ काली मिर्च ने यूरोप को समंदर पार खींचा और डच वी.ओ.सी. ने किलों, समझौतों और तोपों से राज किया।

panels.shot: medium interior of a dim palace hall with maps and palm-leaf records
panels.action: Inside a lamplit Travancore palace hall, Marthanda Varma leans over a floor map marked with forts and rivers, palm-leaf records and Dutch-style ledgers scattered beside ritual lamps.

dialogue.text: Then came Marthanda Varma of Travancore, who saw pepper not just as spice but as a weapon, and began folding the small chiefdoms of south Kerala into a single command.

i18n.hi: फिर आया त्रावणकोर का मार्तान्द वर्मा, जिसने मिर्च को मसाला नहीं, हथियार देखा — और दक्षिण केरल के छोटे नायकों को एक कमान में जोड़ना शुरू किया।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide with Dutch and Travancore lines facing off near a fort
panels.action: On a grassy field before a low coastal fort, Travancore soldiers in disciplined ranks stand opposite Dutch troops and local allies, with Marthanda Varma on a war elephant in the rear, hand raised in calm command.

dialogue.text: The Dutch, used to swaying princes with loans and musket fire, met him in war. Forts fell, allies changed sides, and their victories shrank into costly stalemates.

i18n.hi: कर्ज और बंदूकों से राजकुमारों को हिलाने के आदी डच, उससे जंग में भिड़े। किले गिरे, दोस्त बदल गए, और उनकी जीतें महँगी जड़ता में बदल गईं।

panels.shot: interior wide of a VOC council room in Cochin, tense and shadowed
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged VOC council hall at Cochin, Dutch officials in worn coats sit around a heavy table piled with ledgers and letters, a map of Malabar behind them showing shrinking Dutch influence.

dialogue.text: In Cochin, VOC records tell of a different fear: war costs, declining pepper, fort upkeep, and a Travancore that refused to be steered by Company promises.

i18n.hi: कोच्चि में, वी.ओ.सी. के कागज़ों में और डर लिखा है: जंग का खर्च, घटती मिर्च, किलों की रखवाली, और एक त्रावणकोर जो कम्पनी की बातों से नहीं मुड़ता।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Marthanda Varma in council with local merchants
panels.action: Marthanda Varma sits cross-legged on a low throne, listening as finely dressed Syrian Christian merchants and local officials unfurl palm-leaf contracts, while a scribe notes terms nearby.

dialogue.text: Travancore answered not only with steel, but with contracts. The king licensed Syrian Christian merchants and others as intermediaries, pulling pepper flows under royal eyes.

i18n.hi: त्रावणकोर ने सिर्फ तलवार से नहीं, कागज़ से भी जवाब दिया। राजा ने सिरियाई ईसाई व्यापारियों और दूसरों को दलाल बनाया, मिर्च की धाराओं को राज की नज़र में खींच लिया।

panels.shot: montage-style wide of warehouses and boats loading pepper under official supervision
panels.action: A busy riverside scene shows government-marked warehouses, officials with tally sticks overseeing sacks of pepper being weighed and loaded onto country boats, while merchants negotiate in shaded verandahs.

dialogue.text: The policy was pragmatic. Whoever could move pepper efficiently—through backwaters, godowns and markets—was drawn into the state’s system, binding trade to the crown rather than to Dutch forts.

i18n.hi: नीति बिल्कुल कामचलाऊ थी। जो भी मिर्च को सही से चला सके — बैकवॉटर, गोदाम, बाज़ार से — उसे राज्य के ढाँचे में बाँध दिया, ताकि व्यापार डच किलों नहीं, ताज से जुड़ जाए।

panels.shot: wide of English factory at Anjengo with Union Jack and palm trees
panels.action: A fortified English factory at Anjengo stands on a sandy spit, the Union Jack flying above, with small local boats moored nearby and palm trees bending in the sea breeze.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, the English at Anjengo, Edava and Vizhinjam kept their small factories alive. Travancore watched them, taxed them, but saw them as useful counterweights in a coast crowded with foreigners.

i18n.hi: उधर अंजेन्गो, एदवा और विजिंजम में अंग्रेज़ अपनी छोटी फैक्ट्रियाँ बचाए रहे। त्रावणकोर उन्हें देखता, टैक्स लेता, पर विदेशी भीड़ में उन्हें तौल-मोल के संतुलन की तरह रखता।

panels.shot: closer interior of a VOC clerk writing by lamplight, ledgers open
panels.action: A tired VOC clerk bends over a ledger by lamplight, writing a report as the shadows of empty storerooms fall through the open window behind him.

dialogue.text: VOC letters from the 1740s and early 1750s speak of pepper shortages, money drained by garrisons, and a king who refused to honour old terms that had once humbled smaller chiefs.

i18n.hi: १७४० के दशक और शुरुआती १७५० की वी.ओ.सी. चिट्ठियाँ मिर्च की कमी, छावनियों में उड़ता पैसा, और ऐसे राजा की शिकायत करती हैं जो पुराने, छोटे सरदारों को झुकाने वाले समझौतों को मानने से इंकार करता था।

panels.shot: dramatic interior wide of a Travancore hall prepared for envoys
panels.action: A Travancore audience hall in Mavelikkara is readied with rugs, betel trays and ceremonial lamps, as Marthanda Varma sits poised, attendants flanking him, awaiting the approach of foreign envoys.

dialogue.text: By 1753, both sides were tired. Marthanda Varma held the field, the Dutch held the sea—but neither could afford endless war. So they agreed to meet at Mavelikkara.

i18n.hi: १७५३ तक दोनों थक चुके थे। मैदान पर मार्तान्द वर्मा का राज, समंदर पर डच की पकड़ — पर कोई भी अनंत जंग नहीं झेल सकता था। तय हुआ, मुलाकात मावेलिक्कारा में होगी।

panels.shot: medium wide of Dutch envoys entering the hall to meet Marthanda Varma
panels.action: Dutch envoys in formal coats and hats, escorted by Travancore officials, step carefully into the hall where Marthanda Varma sits upright, his gaze steady as they bow.

dialogue.text: The treaty text, preserved in both VOC and Travancore records, shows how far the world had turned: it is a European company that now comes as supplicant to an Indian king.

i18n.hi: संधि का कागज़, जो वी.ओ.सी. और त्रावणकोर दोनों के रिकॉर्ड में है, दिखाता है कि दुनिया कितनी बदल चुकी थी: अब एक यूरोपीय कम्पनी एक भारतीय राजा के दरबार में फरियादी बन कर आती है।

panels.shot: tight medium on a mat with the treaty palm-leaves spread out between parties
panels.action: On a woven mat between the parties, a neat stack of palm-leaf strips lies unrolled, a Travancore scribe pointing to a clause as both Dutch and royal representatives listen.

dialogue.text: Clause by clause, they reshaped power: the Dutch would no longer meddle in Travancore politics, nor support its enemies, ending a long habit of backing rival chiefs.

i18n.hi: शर्त दर शर्त, ताकत फिर से बाँटी गई: डच अब त्रावणकोर की राजनीति में हाथ नहीं डालेंगे, न उसके दुश्मनों को सहारा देंगे — प्रतिद्वंद्वी सरदारों को पालने की पुरानी आदत खत्म।

panels.shot: close-up on Marthanda Varma’s composed face as he listens, lamplight on his features
panels.action: An intimate close-up shows Marthanda Varma’s face in lamplight, eyes calm yet intent, as a translator murmurs Dutch words in his ear.

dialogue.text: The treaty bound the VOC to respect Travancore’s conquests. Their forts would stand, but their hands were tied. The king’s new frontiers were now lines the Company could not cross.

i18n.hi: संधि ने वी.ओ.सी. को त्रावणकोर की जीतें मानने पर बाँध दिया। उनके किले रहेंगे, पर हाथ बँधे होंगे। राजा की नई सरहदें वे रेखाएँ बन गईं जिन्हें कम्पनी पार नहीं कर सकती।

panels.shot: medium focus on merchants and officials in the hall discussing pepper obligations
panels.action: Syrian Christian merchants and Travancore revenue officials confer in a corner of the hall, gesturing toward palm-leaf lists of pepper quantities and delivery points.

dialogue.text: Pepper, too, was tamed by clauses. The treaty fixed Travancore’s obligation to supply pepper to the VOC, but now on royal terms, through licensed intermediaries already woven into the kingdom’s economy.

i18n.hi: काली मिर्च भी शर्तों से काबू में आई। संधि ने वी.ओ.सी. को मिर्च देने की त्रावणकोर की ज़िम्मेदारी तय की, पर अब राजा की शर्तों पर, उन्हीं लाइसेंसी दलालों के ज़रिए जो पहले से राज्य की अर्थव्यवस्था में बुने गए थे।

panels.shot: medium wide of a British factor being reassured by Travancore official near a coastal factory
panels.action: Near a seaside factory wall bearing English architecture, a Travancore official speaks with a British factor, while guards stand at an easy distance and fishing boats glide by.

dialogue.text: The document also named others. English factories at Anjengo, Edava and Vizhinjam were to be left undisturbed, a clear signal that Travancore would manage foreign rivals without letting one destroy the rest.

i18n.hi: कागज़ में और नाम भी थे। अंजेन्गो, एदवा और विजिंजम की अंग्रेज़ फैक्ट्रियों को न छेड़ने का वादा हुआ — साफ इशारा कि त्रावणकोर विदेशी टक्कर खुद सँभालेगा, किसी एक को बाकी सब को निगलने नहीं देगा।

panels.shot: dramatic medium on Marthanda Varma gesturing to a Dutch representative about war material
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, seated yet commanding, lifts his hand toward a crate of muskets and cannon barrels while a Dutch representative, uneasy, nods agreement.

dialogue.text: Most striking of all, the Dutch agreed to supply war material to the very king they had failed to defeat, turning their own arsenals into tools of Travancore’s defence.

i18n.hi: सबसे चौंकाने वाली बात, डच ने उसी राजा को युद्ध सामग्री देने पर हामी भरी जिसे वे हरा नहीं सके थे — अपनी ही हथियारागार को त्रावणकोर की ढाल में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: close on Marthanda Varma’s mouth as he speaks quietly to an aide
panels.action: A close view shows Marthanda Varma leaning toward a trusted aide, his lips forming calm, measured words while the hall’s murmurs fade into the background.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma
dialogue.text: We fight less with swords now, and more with terms and seals.

i18n.hi: अब तलवार से कम, मुहरों और शर्तों से ज़्यादा लड़ाई होती है।

panels.shot: wide harbour shot of Dutch ships still anchored but quieter, with Travancore guards present
panels.action: A harbour scene at Cochin shows Dutch ships still anchored, smaller than before, as Travancore soldiers and officials move confidently along the quays among local traders.

dialogue.text: The Dutch did not vanish overnight. Their ships still took pepper, their factors still bargained—but after Mavelikkara, they did so as traders in a kingdom’s shadow, not as masters of its rulers.

i18n.hi: डच एक झटके में नहीं गायब हुए। उनके जहाज़ अब भी मिर्च लेते रहे, उनके कारकुन मोलभाव करते रहे — पर मावेलिक्कारा के बाद, वे यह सब एक राज्य की परछाई में करते थे, उसके शासकों के मालिक बनकर नहीं।

panels.shot: montage wide blending a modern Kerala backwater with a ghosted overlay of old forts and ships
panels.action: A serene modern Kerala backwater with houseboats and coconut groves is overlaid faintly by ghostly outlines of old forts and square-rigged ships, suggesting layers of time.

dialogue.text: The Treaty of Mavelikkara did not end Europeans on the coast, but it ended Dutch power in Travancore—showing that in a world of cannon, a treaty could redraw empires more deeply than a battle.

i18n.hi: मावेलिक्कारा की संधि ने तट से यूरोपीय को नहीं मिटाया, पर त्रावणकोर में डच ताकत तोड़ दी — दिखा दिया कि तोपों की दुनिया में भी, एक कागज़ की संधि कभी-कभी जंग से गहरी सीमा खींच सकती है।

title_i18n.en: The Treaty of Mavelikkara Ends Dutch Power
title_i18n.hi: मावेलिक्कारा की संधि से डच सत्ता खत्म

subtitle_i18n.hi: काली मिर्च ने बंदूकें खरीदीं, साम्राज्य गिर पड़ा
